From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@helixai.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@helixai.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: RFP: Dedicated Inference - Sizing Questionnaire

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking our RFP. We're evaluating several providers for a dedicated inference tier to support our conversational agents and multi-turn retrieval pipeline. Attached is our standard sizing questionnaire — can you complete the sections on GPU sizing, throughput targets, and reservation model? High level:

- Peak expected QPS (inference requests): ~150 req/s (burst to 300 for launches)
- Typical prompt + response: 1.5k tokens average (prompt 700 / generation 800)
- Model target: open-weight family, fidelity roughly comparable to 7B–70B LLMs depending on use-case (we plan to stage two models: a high-throughput 7B-ish smaller model for low latency, and a 70B for higher fidelity tasks).
- Latency requirements: p95 end-to-end generation < 600ms for 7B; < 1800ms for 70B (where practicable).

Can you also call out recommended GPU mixes for a two-pool dedicated reservation (stable baseline + burst pool), and clarify what reserve commitments we'd need for predictable throughput under your autoscaling and fallback policies?

Appreciate a completed worksheet and any assumptions baked into your sizing. Would like your initial answers by EOD Thursday, May 20.

Thanks,
Liam
Procurement Lead | HelixAI
Attachments: helix-rfp-questions.pdf (PDF, 420KB)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>

Hi Liam —

Thanks — we reviewed the questionnaire and put together a preliminary sizing worksheet attached (redwood-dedicated-sizing-worksheet-v1.xlsx). High-level summary up front so your team can review quickly:

- Recommendation: two dedicated pools — Baseline Pool: 10x A100-80GB equivalent for sustained throughput and KV-cache heavy workloads; Burst Pool: 4x H100-80GB (or equivalent L40/H100) to handle launch spikes and low-latency critical paths. Total suggested reservation: 14 GPUs.
- Assumptions: 70B model in 4-bit quantized form with KV cache for multi-turn; typical generation length = 800 tokens; batching at runtime yields effective throughput of ~6 tokens/ms per GPU for 70B quantized on A100-80GB; smaller 7B family runs ~4x higher throughput per GPU.
- Expected steady-state QPS coverage: Baseline pool as sized covers ~120 req/s for mixed traffic (weighted 60% small model / 40% large model). Burst pool absorbs spikes to ~300 req/s sustained for ~30-minute windows before autoscale billing.
- Latency: with suggested mix and continuous batching, p95 for 7B target is ~280–420ms; for quantized 70B we estimate p95 1.2–1.6s under mixed load.
- Autoscale model & fallback: reserve baseline pool for committed throughput; automatic warm-up to burst GPUs when queue depth exceeds threshold; policy includes automatic fallback to smaller model family when queue > 2x baseline for fidelity-tolerant requests.

I've CC'd Rishi for sign-off on the GPU mixing and cost assumptions. Attached worksheet includes per-model concurrency, batch-size, token-rate assumptions, and slot-level packings.

Next steps: if the numbers look reasonable we can lock a working call and I will produce a short appendix that maps these GPU counts to expected monthly committed spend and on-demand burst exposure.

Best,
Priya Natarajan

Priya / Vivek —

Quick read of Priya's draft: good baseline. A few asks before we finalize numbers to customer:

1) GPU choice rationale: call out explicit perf ratios and packing expectations (e.g., 70B quantized on A100-80 gives X tokens/sec; H100 gives ~1.6x for same quantized binary on our runtime). We should present both performance and cost delta and recommend the mix that minimizes committed spend while preserving p95 SLAs.

2) Reservation sizing logic: the questionnaire expects guaranteed QPS for peak windows. Let's propose: commit to Baseline = capacity for 95th percentile sustained (we should ask HelixAI for 30/60/90-day historical traffic if possible). Then offer a burst contract for up to additional 200% capacity billed as usage. Also note warm pool lead times (cold start for new model + cache fill is ~3–6 minutes).

3) Recovery/failover: add note about graceful degradation — route to smaller model or region fallback. Also mention KV cache replication across GPUs in pool to avoid repeated warm-ups for short-lived sessions.

I can sign off on the numbers if you quantify the A100 vs H100 per-GPU throughput table and a conservative headroom factor (1.2x) for unexpected spikes.

-Rishi
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: RE: RFP: Dedicated Inference - Sizing Questionnaire

Thanks Rishi — responded inline in the updated worksheet and added the explicit performance table you asked for. Summary of the table (copied into email for quick reference):

- A100-80GB (4-bit quantized 70B): ~120k tokens/s aggregate per GPU (approx 6 tokens/ms), practical concurrent in-flight tokens limited by KV cache and sequence length; effective request throughput ~10–12 70B requests/sec per GPU at avg 800-token generation when batching aggressively.
- H100-80GB (same quantized model): ~1.6x token/s -> ~192k tokens/s aggregate; effective 70B requests/sec ~16–19 per GPU under same batching profile.
- 7B family (quantized): ~45–60 7B requests/sec per A100 GPU (much higher due to smaller compute).

Packing & reservation recommendation v2: Baseline pool (commit) = 8x A100-80GB + 2x H100-80GB (accounts for steady multi-model mix and leaves headroom). Burst pool (on top of baseline) = 4x H100-80GB (on-demand or reserved for short windows). Total reserved GPUs suggested: 10 (8 A100 + 2 H100) with optional burst contract to reach 14 for launches. This reduces committed spend while meeting Helix's stated p95 SLAs with ~20% safety headroom.

I've updated worksheet version to v2 and attached an SLA appendix doc. If you're good, I'll send this back to Helix with a short explanation of the assumptions and a proposed call time.

—Priya

Hi Liam —

Appreciate the questionnaire. Attaching an updated worksheet (redwood-dedicated-sizing-worksheet-v2.xlsx) and a short SLA appendix (redwood-sla-term-sheet.pdf). Key points and final recommendations:

- Recommended committed reservation: 8x A100-80GB + 2x H100-80GB (10 GPUs total). Baseline covers ~95th percentile sustained mixed traffic (est. 120–140 req/s for weighted mix) with continuous KV caching and batching as configured.
- Burst strategy: contract to allow an additional 4x H100-80GB for short windows (launches, promotions) which gives effective burst capacity to ~300 req/s. Burst can be on-demand billed usage or reserved short-term (30–90 day commitments).
- Operational assumptions:
  - Warm-up for cold model deployments ~3–6 minutes for KV cache; we recommend pre-warming during launches.
  - Autoscale policy: trigger additional GPUs when request queue depth exceeds 2x baseline or average p95 start to exceed target SLA for 3 consecutive minutes.
  - Graceful fallback: route fidelity-tolerant traffic to 7B family when overall queue > 2x baseline.

Cost & contract: the attached worksheet maps GPUs to expected monthly committed spend and a sensitivity table for on-demand burst usage.

Would love to schedule a 45-minute call next week to walk through the worksheet and lock down a draft SOW. Would Tue 25 May at 11am PT or Wed 26 May at 9am PT work?
